intro: Pench Tiger Reserve covers the forests of the Pench river valley on the border of Madhya Pradesh (Seoni and Chhindwara districts) and Maharashtra (Nagpur district), where each state manages its own part. The landscape of teak and mixed forest, with the river and the Totladoh reservoir at its heart, is the country Rudyard Kipling drew on for The Jungle Book.

The reserve is known for tigers, leopards and wild dogs (dhole), large herds of chital and gaur, and rich birdlife. Its easy access from Nagpur makes it popular for a short safari break. The Madhya Pradesh side is the more visited; the Maharashtra side, through gates such as Sillari, is quieter.
quickAnswer: Pench Tiger Reserve, on the Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra border, is reached from Nagpur, about two to three hours by road. On the Madhya Pradesh side, the core zones are entered through the Turia, Karmajhiri and Jamtara gates, with buffer gates such as Khawasa and Rukhad. Core zones open from 1 October to 30 June; buffers can run in the monsoon. Book on the official MP Online forest portal up to 120 days ahead.
takeaways: Pench straddles Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra; each side has its own gates and booking.
Turia is the busiest Madhya Pradesh gate and the only one with canter safaris.
Core zones close from 1 July to 30 September; some buffer zones stay open.
The Madhya Pradesh side is closed for afternoon safaris on Wednesdays.
Nagpur is the nearest airport and railway hub.

rows: Most popular; jeeps and canters; many lodges nearby
Useful when core permits are sold out

items.name: Tigers and other predators
body: Pench became famous in the 2010s for a tigress known as Collarwali, which raised a record number of cubs. Leopards, dhole (Indian wild dogs), jungle cats and sloth bears are also seen.

items.name: Herbivores
body: Chital are abundant, along with sambar, nilgai, gaur and wild boar.

items.name: Birds
body: The mix of forest, grassland and water supports a rich bird list, including peafowl, crested serpent eagles, Indian pitta in season and waterbirds on the reservoir.

sections.heading: Safari details
list: Two shifts a day: early morning and afternoon, with timings that change with the season.
Jeeps (gypsies) carry up to six visitors with a driver and a registered guide.
Canter safaris run only from Turia gate, with a small number of vehicles.
Madhya Pradesh side: afternoon safaris are closed on Wednesdays.
Book core permits early for weekends, holidays and April to June.

sections.heading: Booking
paras: Permits for the Madhya Pradesh side are sold on the MP Online forest department portal, opening up to 120 days in advance; the Maharashtra side is booked through Maharashtra's forest department. Lodges near Turia usually help with bookings. Use only the official portals or trusted operators; many unofficial sites imitate them.

sections.heading: Tips for a better Pench safari
list: Book at least three drives; each one covers only part of one zone.
Mix core and buffer drives. Buffer zones are cheaper, less crowded and often productive.
Ask your lodge which zones have had recent activity, but treat it as a guide, not a promise.
Spend time on birds, dhole and smaller animals; the drive is worthwhile even without a tiger.
Carry a light jacket even in March; open jeeps are cold before sunrise.
Leave a rest day between drives if you are travelling with young children.

rows: Pleasant and green; cold mornings in December and January
Hot; forest thins and animals gather at water; good for sightings
Core closed; some buffer safaris in the monsoon

sections.heading: Getting there and where to stay
list: Nagpur, with an airport and major railway station, is about two to three hours by road from Turia.
Seoni is the nearest town on the Madhya Pradesh side; Jabalpur is further north.
Most lodges and resorts cluster around Turia gate; some are near Karmajhiri and Khawasa.
Combine Pench with Kanha (about five hours by road) or Tadoba (about five to six hours).

rows: Arrive from Nagpur by midday; afternoon buffer or core safari from Turia
Morning core safari; rest; afternoon safari from a different gate
A final morning safari, then return to Nagpur or continue to Kanha

safety: Sightings are never guaranteed; tigers are wild and move widely.
Stay inside the vehicle and follow the guide's instructions.
Keep noise down and do not feed animals.
Carry the ID used for booking.
Drive carefully on the highway at night; wildlife crosses the roads near the reserve.
packing: Sunscreen, hat and water for summer

faqs.a: On the Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra border, in Seoni and Chhindwara (MP) and Nagpur (Maharashtra) districts.

faqs.q: Which is the best gate in Pench?
faqs.a: Turia is the most popular core gate on the Madhya Pradesh side; Karmajhiri and Jamtara are quieter.
Core zones close from 1 July to 30 September. The Madhya Pradesh side closes for afternoon safaris on Wednesdays.

faqs.q: How far is Pench from Nagpur?
faqs.a: About two to three hours by road to Turia.

faqs.q: Is Pench the Jungle Book forest?
faqs.a: Rudyard Kipling set The Jungle Book in the Seoni area, and Pench's forests are often associated with it.
